chunks.title: CLO2021 Year of the Ox Special Live Broadcast ~ Mastering Print Operations in CLO ~ Wishing Everyone a New Year of Ox Times Ox!
chunks.content: # CLO2021 Year of the Ox Special Live Broadcast ## Mastering Print Operations in CLO for New Year Designs This document covers detailed procedures and techniques for creating and customizing clothing designs in CLO, focusing on print operations, fabric manipulation, and 3D simulation. Key topics include garment pattern editing, applying textures and stickers, managing layers and materials, using the print editor, designing complex elements like cow ears and feet, and advanced rendering techniques such as hair and color change effects. --- ## Importing and Preparing Garment Patterns: Cow's Feet and Ears This section explains how to import garment patterns and edit details such as the cow's feet and ears for 3D simulation in CLO, emphasizing version management, line conversion, sewing, and shape adjustments. - Import the garment pattern (e.g., down jacket and pants) and locate the hat pattern with pre-drawn cow's feet positions. - Convert the baseline to an internal line, then create a new version for faster processing by freezing unused versions. - Measure lengths precisely (e.g., cow's foot side length 76.4 mm) and convert straight lines to curves using Ctrl for smooth shape adjustment. - Adjust the shape of the cow's foot board, comparing it to sandpaper texture; modify size to fit design requirements. - Reduce particle diameter on the simulation board to avoid damage and improve stitching quality. - Sew half of the cow's foot to one side of the hat pattern, then add it to the outside of the hat. - Simulate the sewing and adjust the size manually if the cow's foot looks too large or flat. - Copy (Ctrl+D) and align the cow's foot to the opposite side for symmetry. - Harden the board or add a sticky layer with adjustable hardness to make the cow's foot appear fuller and maintain shape without permanent hardening. - For cow ears, measure the internal line length (e.g., 47.5 mm) and draw a peach-shaped pattern. - Extend board edges by 25mm on both sides, add straight line points, and sew edges together using the editor tool. - Attach cow ears to the hat pattern, adjust position and length using the grid tool in the 3D window. - Create a colon layer (layer duplication) for double layering of ears to achieve a bulging effect. - Harden or soften layers as needed to balance shape and flexibility. - Place cow ears and feet on separate fabric pieces for customized material application. --- ## Applying and Customizing Textures and Stickers Using the Print Editor This section covers the use of CLO’s print editor for adding, editing, and layering textures and stickers on garments, including adjustment of size, position, color, and blending modes. - Open the print editor from the fabric or texture section to add new textures or stickers. - Add textures in layers similar to Photoshop, where layers can be locked or deleted. - Adjust texture parameters such as grid size, transparency, color mixing, flatness, and extension to other sides.

chunks.content: --- ## Applying and Customizing Textures and Stickers Using the Print Editor This section covers the use of CLO’s print editor for adding, editing, and layering textures and stickers on garments, including adjustment of size, position, color, and blending modes. - Open the print editor from the fabric or texture section to add new textures or stickers. - Add textures in layers similar to Photoshop, where layers can be locked or deleted. - Adjust texture parameters such as grid size, transparency, color mixing, flatness, and extension to other sides. - Import transparent PNG stickers (e.g., traditional New Year warrior, flowers) and adjust their size and position. - Use the right-hand corner controls to fine-tune sticker placement and scaling. - Manage overlapping stickers using different blend modes like normal, flat slope, etc., enabling creative print designs. - Duplicate stickers and layers to create complex combinations and patterns. - Use color meters to match sticker colors with fabric tones and adjust transparency and flatness for desired effects. - Apply colors to stickers to create multi-color effects; combine colors like red, green, and gold for auspicious designs. - Always click "Apply" after edits to ensure changes are reflected in the garment. - Generate continuous four-sided stickers automatically for seamless fabric export. - Use "Add Print on Back" to add patterns to the reverse side of fabrics, managed similarly to front textures. - Adjust pattern rotation, scaling, and color within the print editor for precise design placement. - Use traditional Chinese motifs (jade, flowers) to enhance festive designs and experiment with metallic materials for gold effects. --- ## Simulation and Rendering Techniques: Particle Diameter, Layering, and Hair Effects This section details how to optimize simulation settings and material properties for realistic garment rendering, including particle diameter adjustments, layering for fullness, and advanced hair/fur material creation. - Reduce particle diameter (e.g., to 5) to speed up simulations and improve garment behavior. - Add multiple layers (e.g., two or three) for parts like cow’s feet to increase volume and realism. - Use the sticky layer with adjustable hardness to maintain shape without excessive hardening. - For fluffy or furry effects on elements (e.g., the cow figure), change fabric type to fur or hair. - Adjust hair length, density, and thickness parameters to achieve desired softness and volume. - Shorten or lengthen hair and increase density (e.g., density from 800 to 1000) for natural effects. - Use a default black-and-white mask image to control hair growth areas precisely: white indicates hair presence; black excludes hair. - Rendering settings must be adjusted to visualize hair correctly: - Increase light source intensity and rendering quality for bright white hair appearance. - Adjust medium and highest light properties to enhance hair brightness and detail. - Hair rendering requires patience, adjusting properties individually for the best effect. - Use multi-angle rendering checks to verify appearance from different perspectives.

small or detailed patterns may have grid or snapping issues. - For complex shapes like cow’s feet, add middle points on curves to adjust size and shape precisely. - Use inner and outer layering techniques to improve 3D volume and sewing quality. - If cow’s feet appear flat or collapsed, check if hardening or sticky layers are applied correctly. - Sticky layers should be chosen with appropriate hardness depending on the area (harder for main body, softer for collars or pockets). - Pressure inflow can be used but may not be as effective as sticky layers for fullness. - Ensure sewing lines are correctly connected and delete unnecessary lines to avoid simulation errors. - When applying fur or hair materials, adjust bending strength to control stiffness or flow of hair strands. - Use silk materials and adjust color intensity for realistic skin or fabric surfaces. - Regularly save and freeze unused pattern versions to improve software performance during complex simulations. --- ## Summary of Key Materials and Design Elements - **Cow’s Feet and Ears:** Custom patterns with layered boards, sewn and shaped with sticky/hardened layers. - **Print Editor:** Layer-based texture and sticker application with color, transparency, and blend mode controls. - **Particle Diameter:** Reduced values improve simulation speed and garment detail fidelity.
